prompt:
You are a credit rating analyst. Using only the information below and general knowledge predating 2026-02-13, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify).
Valid answers (choose exactly one): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Company information (as of 2026-02-13):
| Current ratio           | 1.44 |
| Retained earnings       | 65,448M |
| Current liabilities     | 36,558M |
| Current assets          | 52,485M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 21,318M |
| Total liabilities       | 77,267M |
| Total assets            | 98,585M |
| EBIT / operating income | 2,660M |
| Revenue                 | 19,133M |
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company shows solid liquidity (current ratio 1.44) and positive operating earnings, but exhibits relatively high leverage (debt to equity around 3.6) with substantial liabilities relative to equity. Absence of interest coverage data keeps downside risk only moderately contained, suggesting investment-grade but not strong credit quality.

DECISION: BBB+
